verdict_reason: Ahrefs has a broad, well-documented public REST API v3 with API-key authentication, plus OAuth 2.0/PKCE via Ahrefs Connect and a vendor-hosted MCP server. However, API credentials require an eligible paid plan (Lite at $129/mo includes API access; the Starter tier has no API units), so there is no free self-serve developer tier for the general API. Multi-user OAuth integrations additionally go through the Ahrefs Connect approval program.
main_blocker: Paid Ahrefs plan required (API access from Lite, $129/mo; Starter has 0 API units); multi-user OAuth needs Ahrefs Connect approval
open_questions: Official vendor SDKs: no vendor-maintained client libraries were found in the fetched docs; confirm whether any official SDKs exist.
Webhooks/event callbacks: no webhook documentation surfaced in the fetched docs; confirm whether Ahrefs offers webhooks.
Sandbox: no dedicated sandbox/test environment is documented; Ahrefs only documents free test queries against production targets.

Free/public endpoints: a search snippet mentions a 'Public' endpoint group that may not require an Ahrefs subscription; that page was not in the fetched sources—verify whether any no-subscription API access exists.
Ahrefs Connect admission criteria and review timeline are not detailed; multi-user OAuth apps must be publicly available and are admitted at Ahrefs' sole discretion.
No community/third-party MCP servers were found in the provided evidence; only the official hosted MCP server is documented.

MCP endpoint: the docs publish the Streamable HTTP endpoint https://api.ahrefs.com/mcp/mcp, but a plain GET fetch returned HTTP 405; docs also state the external MCP endpoint is not a general-purpose programmatic API.
Auth: the public API Introduction documents API keys, while the Ahrefs Connect OAuth guide documents OAuth 2.0/PKCE; the two mechanisms are documented separately rather than on one page.
Rate limits: dynamic throttling may also return HTTP 429 in addition to the fixed 60 requests/minute cap; the quoted clause covers only the fixed cap.
API versioning: docs refer to API v3, but no separate public API deprecation/versioning policy was located beyond the Ahrefs Connect terms.
